title: Corn, sweet, yellow and white kernels, fresh, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet corn with yellow and white kernels is a fresh, unprocessed ear harvested at peak maturity. The kernels have a tender, mildly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. Corn can be eaten raw and is also used in salads, side dishes, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet corn belongs to Zea mays var. saccharata and is cultivated specifically for fresh consumption.
Yellow and white kernels differ mainly in carotenoid content; yellow kernels are rich in lutein, while white kernels have a milder taste.
Corn is one of the oldest cultivated crops, domesticated over 7,000 years ago in Mexico.
Sweet corn contains more sugar and less starch than field corn, giving it a juicier bite.
In the United States, more than 90 million tons of fresh corn are consumed each year.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Sweet corn provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in yellow kernels protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6 and folate
items.content: These B‑vitamins are involved in amino‑acid metabolism and support nervous‑system health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Sweet corn is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to digestive issues.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Because of its natural sugars, sweet corn should be consumed in moderation by people with diabetes.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Commercially grown corn may contain pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the kernels straight from the cob, either raw or after a quick boil or grill for a softer texture. Sweet corn works well in salads, smoothies, juices, and as a side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh ears in the refrigerator, wrapped in plastic, for 3–5 days. For longer storage, remove the kernels and freeze them in an airtight bag.
